title.en: The role of the judiciary in our society

text.en: The Preamble promises every citizen social, economic and political justice. Who makes sure that promise is kept when people disagree?

Justice is essential for peace and harmony, and disputes arise in every society between people, groups and governments.
The judiciary is one of the three pillars of government, independent of the legislature and the executive.
An independent judiciary decides disputes fairly, protects the Constitution and rights, and checks that governments follow the law.
The structure is a pyramid: the Supreme Court at the top, High Courts in the states, and District and subordinate courts below.
Courts hear civil cases, such as disputes about property, and criminal cases, such as theft or violence.
A person unhappy with a decision can appeal to a higher court.
The Supreme Court is the guardian of the Constitution and fundamental rights, and can strike down laws that violate it.
Public Interest Litigation (PIL) lets any citizen approach the court for the benefit of the public.
Alternative ways to settle disputes include dialogue, mediation, conciliation, arbitration and Lok Adalats, which are faster and cheaper.
Legal aid helps poor people get a lawyer, so that justice is available to all.

problem.en: A property dispute can go through which courts?

text.en: It starts in a District Court.
An appeal can go to the High Court.
The final appeal is the Supreme Court.

prompt.en: Why must the judiciary be independent?

requiredIdeas.en: To check the government and protect rights.

points.en: The judiciary decides disputes and protects rights.
Courts: Supreme Court, High Courts, District Courts.
Mediation and Lok Adalats are alternatives.
